To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the establishment of interaction between parental regulatory networks of the allopolyploidy is accompanied by homoeolog-specific transcription of genes involved in photosynthetic and protein synthesis pathways.
the majority of genes are expressed at the mid-parental level in allohexaploid, while a minority are up-regulated or down-regulated.
allopolyploidy in wheat leads to a massive up- and down regulation of homoeologous genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the molecular mechanisms of gene expression regulation during the formation of allopolyploidy.
the analysis of homoeology-specific gene expression and the role of homoeologous gene expression in the establishment of allopolyploidy.
the evolution of gene regulation in allopolypoids and provides insights into the mechanisms of gene expression and genome evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of the wheat genome is not subject to non-additive expression in the allohexaploid.
the majority of genes are regulated additively, but that there is a small number of non-additive genes which can be attributed to the parental genotypes and/or the hybridization process.
the expression of homoeologs is not simply additive in allopolypoids, but rather is highly biased towards up-regulation of the parental type of gene activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
allopolyploid genome evolution in wheat is driven by homoeolog-specific changes in gene expression.
allopolyploid genomes are not additive, and that they are not even additive.
the wheat allopolyploidy is accompanied by homoeolog-specific transcription bias and that the wheat allohexaploid transcriptome can be described as a mosaic of parental gene expression patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parental genotypes have a significant effect on gene expression in the allohexaploid.

the establishment of allopolyploidy does not lead to the complete loss of parental gene expression, as was proposed in the past, but rather to the establishment of new regulatory networks that are biased toward the parental type of gene regulation.
homoeolog-specific expression is a common phenomenon in wheat, and that it is a consequence of the differences between parental genotypes.
